question: How do hyperscale engineering architectures (Google SRE, Google DeepMind, Microsoft Systems, AWS CloudWatch/AppConfig, Meta Infrastructure, OpenAI, Anthropic MCP, Netflix Conductor, Palantir Foundry, SEI CMU, OWASP) implement self-observation, capability gap detection, architecture fitness auditing, simulated evolution proposals, and self-modification protection governance?
scope: Control Plane self-observation, 10-state self-assessment classification, capability and governance gap detection, 18-state evolution proposal lifecycle, meta-meta-verification, and self-modification protection gates
claims: A self-evaluating control plane must maintain a strict separation between observation/proposal and physical implementation authorization.
Self-modification protection must forbid unapproved mutations of foundational governance, constitution, security write barriers, and verifier independence rules.
evidence: Google Borg/Autopilot and Kubernetes reconciliation controllers use dry-run simulation loops before applying infrastructure policy changes.
AWS AppConfig and Netflix Canary deployments enforce automated regression detection gates to roll back degraded releases.
observations: Evolution proposals must be scored against multi-dimensional criteria (quality, safety, performance, evidence strength) without provider bias.
Learning loops must generate candidate proposals and evidence records rather than mutating governance rules automatically.
limitations: Self-evolution simulation operates locally in synthetic mode prior to live commercial API activation.
recommendation: Implement Autonomous Self-Evaluation Engine, 18-state Evolution Proposal State Machine, Self-Modification Protection Gate, Meta-Meta-Verification, and Synthetic Self-Evolution Fixtures in EOS Control Plane.
